title: Metarun implementation kickstart and SLA playbook
summary: Intro kickoff for Metarun to validate network, security, and success criteria for Redwood Private/Dedicated evaluation. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share runbook and bench template; Metarun to provide sample load profile and security questionnaire answers. Discussed initial SLA targets (p90 token latency < 350ms for 4k seq) and fallback strategy to hosted model during peak.
next_steps: Alex to send onboarding runbook + VPC checklist by 2027-01-20
Sana to share current infra diagram and sample traffic profile by 2027-01-22
Priya to schedule an SSO/SAML deep dive with Ethan by 2027-01-26
Marcos to open pilot workspace and invite Metarun users by 2027-01-21
action_items: Alex - Share dedicated onboarding runbook (incl. VPC checklist and sample terraform snippets) - due 2027-01-20
Sana - Export historical token/time series for the last 30 days and upload to drive - due 2027-01-22
Ethan - Provide answers to Redwood security questionnaire (initial pass) - due 2027-01-24
Priya - Provision pilot credentials and arrange 60-min SSO session - due 2027-01-26
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-01-17 | Time: 15:00 - 15:58 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marcos Diaz (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Metarun), Sana Qureshi (Metarun), Ethan Park (Metarun), Maya Ortiz (Metarun)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick round of intros? I'm Alex Morgan, AE for Redwood Inference.
[00:08] Jordan Lee: Jordan here, Head of ML Ops at Metarun. We run low-latency pipelines for inference across customers.
[00:15] Sana Qureshi: Sana, platform eng, I own network and infra.
[00:21] Ethan Park: Ethan, security and compliance.
[00:24] Priya Patel: Priya from Redwood SE, I’ll lead the technical onboarding and pilot setup.
[00:30] Marcos Diaz: Marcos, CSM — I'll help with runbooks and timelines.
[00:36] Maya Ortiz: Maya, product, interested in rollout pacing and observability.
[00:45] Alex Morgan: Great. Agenda: network checklist/VPC peering, SLA targets and perf expectations, pilot scope, and security/compliance items. Any additions?
[00:52] Jordan Lee: That covers it — and we want to validate cost vs latency tradeoffs, so please include cost modeling notes.
[01:00] Alex Morgan: Will do. Quick background — Redwood enables hosted, dedicated, and private. For enterprise we usually start with a dedicated pilot or private VPC depending on data residency.
[01:12] Sana Qureshi: We're leaning private (VPC) because of PII pipeline and strict egress rules, but open to dedicated if networking is simpler.
[01:20] Priya Patel: Understood. For Private we provide a control plane handshake plus customer-managed VPC peering or private link. We have sample terraform snippets in the runbook.
[01:30] Ethan Park: On the security side, SOC2 certs are great, but we'll need KMS integration details and audit log retention specifics.
[01:37] Alex Morgan: We'll include KMS/HSM patterns and audit retention options in the security appendix.
[01:42] [00:60] Jordan Lee: Sorry, did you say H-S-M? sometimes transcripts flip letters.
[01:46] Priya Patel: Yeah HSM, hardware security module — for key protection.
[02:00] Alex Morgan: Performance — Jordan, what's your current p90 latency for generation at 4k context?
[02:08] Jordan Lee: On our infra it's around 650ms p90 right now, with bursts hitting 1.2s when we have longer contexts.
[02:16] Priya Patel: For a Dedicated pool we typically hit sub-400ms p90 for 4k with optimized kernels and batching config; depends on model and quantization. We'll share model profiles in the runbook.
[02:26] Sana Qureshi: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching — we have many repeated prompts across sessions.
[02:33] Priya Patel: We have prefix/KV caching built in; caching can reduce effective tokens and cost significantly. We'll propose TTLs and cache key strategies in the pilot config.
[02:43] Maya Ortiz: Can we see telemetry in the console for token-level cost?
[02:47] Marcos Diaz: Yes, Console shows token-level cost, per-route latencies, and trace links. We'll create an access view for Metarun.
[02:55] Ethan Park: About fallback strategies — you mentioned fallback to hosted model under peak, how seamless is that?
[03:02] Priya Patel: We support policy-based routing. If Dedicated capacity is saturated we can route to a hosted variant (potentially different quantization/higher cost) and tag requests so the app sees no error. There is a small delta in latency and occasionally output variance.
[03:18] Jordan Lee: Output variance is acceptable if we have clear SLAs and can do regression checks.
[03:24] Alex Morgan: Speaking of SLAs, for the pilot we're proposing an internal p90 target of 350ms for 4k sequences and an availability SLO of 99.5% — enterprise SLA can be negotiated later.
[03:36] Sana Qureshi: 350ms p90 is ambitious — what's the hardware assumption?
[03:40] Priya Patel: That assumes A100-class or similar and the quantized model stack; we'll include hardware sizing in the runbook. If you're on older GPU, numbers change.
[03:50] Jordan Lee: We'll share our cloud region and current instance types.
[03:54] Alex Morgan: Great. Onboarding steps: 1) network connectivity and peering, 2) pilot dataset and traffic profile, 3) security questionnaire, 4) pilot go/no-go criteria.
[04:06] Maya Ortiz: For go/no-go, we want: p90 latency within 1.2x of target, accuracy within 2% of baseline on our eval prompts, and cost-per-1000-tokens within projected budget.
[04:18] Priya Patel: We'll accept those and map them into the pilot success criteria doc.
[04:24] [04:30] Sana Qureshi: On VPC, what's the preferred approach — peering vs PrivateLink? We have strict egress rules that prefer PrivateLink.
[04:33] Priya Patel: PrivateLink is supported, though setup differs per cloud. We'll include both patterns. For peering we need route tables and NAT config notes.
[04:42] Ethan Park: For audit logs, can you push logs to our SIEM?
[04:45] Marcos Diaz: Yes, we can stream audit logs to S3, and from there you can ingest to Splunk or whatever SIEM you have. We'll document schemas.
[04:54] Jordan Lee: Any blockers from your side?
[04:58] Alex Morgan: None — next step is I share the runbook. Also, we'd like a small benchmark test: Metarun to run a baseline against a tiny sample set, then Redwood will run pilot and we compare.
[05:10] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. We'll put together a 30-minute perf run and share metrics.
[05:14] Priya Patel: On canary rollouts — we recommend starting with 10% of traffic on Dedicated and increase to 100% over two weeks with monitoring thresholds.
[05:24] Maya Ortiz: Two weeks is fine; product wants to see dashboarding and alerts before full ramp.
[05:30] [05:35] Ethan Park: On SSO, we use SAML via Okta. How's integration?
[05:38] Priya Patel: Okta SAML is standard. We have a handoff doc for metadata.xml and required attributes. We'll schedule the SSO session.
[05:46] Sana Qureshi: Network team will need exact CIDR ranges and firewall rules.
[05:50] Alex Morgan: I'll include precise CIDRs in the VPC checklist.
[05:55] Jordan Lee: Regarding cost modeling — will you provide an estimate for token-based pricing under different batching and quantization profiles?
[06:02] Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize has suggested configs: aggressive batching reduces cost but increases latency. We'll provide a matrix with estimated tokens/sec and cost-per-1k for each profile.
[06:12] Alex Morgan: Ok let's map responsibilities and timing — Marcos, can you open the pilot workspace?
[06:18] Marcos Diaz: Yup — I'll provision and invite the listed Metarun users by Friday.
[06:22] Maya Ortiz: Who will own the regression checks? Product or ML Ops?
[06:26] Jordan Lee: ML Ops will run baseline evals, product will validate UX impact.
[06:31] [06:40] Priya Patel: Quick question from tech: what model family are you evaluating?
[06:44] Jordan Lee: We're starting with a LLaMA-variant tuned in-house, ~7B, then a 13B if quality requires.
[06:52] Priya Patel: Good — we'll include quantization profiles and kernel recommendations per family.
[07:00] Alex Morgan: Any procurement concerns?
[07:03] Ethan Park: We'll need contract language for data residency and indemnity. Also we'll run a velo procurement review; timeline depends on legal but pilot can start with an MSA addendum.
[07:14] Alex Morgan: We'll share a starter MSA addendum and the security docs.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: For the pilot, timeline wise we'd like to start pilot infra next week and run for two weeks — is that feasible?
[07:25] Priya Patel: Yes, if we get network access and sample traffic this week we can stand up pilot infra in 5 business days.
[07:33] Sana Qureshi: We'll prioritize the infra diagram to unblock you.
[07:36] Alex Morgan: Ok recap — Redwood sends runbook, VPC checklist, security pack; Metarun sends infra diagram, traffic sample, and security answers. Marcos will provision pilot workspace and Priya will run pilot config once we have data.
[07:52] Maya Ortiz: One more question: observability retention, does Redwood allow custom retention for traces?
[07:56] Marcos Diaz: We have tiered retention; enterprise customers can extend retention as an add-on.
[08:02] Ethan Park: For audit purposes we need 1 year retention on critical audit trails.
[08:06] Alex Morgan: Noted, we'll include retention SLAs and pricing in the docs.
[08:11] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[08:14] Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with materials.
[08:18] [58:00] End of recording.
